Speed Limit Review - 
update 
The Department of Transport carried out a Review of 
Speed Limits nationally and this has resulted in changes 
to the default speed limits for roads in Ireland. These 
changes were signed into law in April 2024.   The 
changes to the legislation will reduce the default speed 
limits on some road categories including:  
 
• 
60km/hr on Rural Local Roads (reduction 
from 80km/hr) 
• 
80km/hr on National Secondary Roads 
(currently 100km/hr) 
• 
30km/hr in Urban Areas (currently 
predominantly 50km/hr). 
 
The implementation of the reduction of a default speed 
limit on Rural Local Roads to 60km/hr is complete.   
 
It is proposed by the National 
Group that implementation of the 
speed limits will be done in phases:  
• 
Phase 1 - Complete 
• 
Phase 2 - Urban Areas  
• 
Phase 3 - Other Special 
Circumstances, schools etc. 
   
Progress on Phase 2 has 
commenced with pre-consultation 
letters issued, and all 3 AGS 
Divisions have been met and 
consulted with. Our 5 District 
Councils have also been met and 
consulted with. Formal consultation 
with AGS and TII is due to 
commence in July. 
 
The nationally set time frame for 
adoption of the new bye-laws is 30th 
October 2026 with the enactment 
date set as 1st March 2027. This is a 
very challenging time frame given 
the nature of the review.

CFRAM FLOOD RELIEF SCHEMES 
Flood Relief Schemes 
Current Update 
Ballina FRS 
The first consultation with the public and stakeholders took place online 
from 8th November – 6th December 2021. The second public consultation 
day was held on 12th June 2025 during which the community were presented 
with five options developed to alleviate flooding including the emerging 
preferred option.  
Significant requests for further information and amendments to the scheme 
were made by attendees.  The design team has undertaken a high-level review 
taking these submissions into consideration.  
Upon selection of the emerging preferred option, the scheme will then 
proceed to Stage II, the planning process, where the preferred option will be 
developed and an application submitted to An Coimisiún Pleanála. 
Holycross FRS 
Stage 1 Option Selection for Holycross FRS is complete. The proposed 
Capital Flood Relief Scheme was not accepted by the benefitting property 
owners. 
Knocklofty FRS 
In July 2024 the OPW approved the Preferred Option in the Options 
Report, which enabled progression of the Knocklofty FRS.  The Preferred 
Option is to construct raised defences on the River Suir to prevent flooding 
with stormwater drainage behind the defences. Total budget of €1.1m.  
This option was presented to the public for feedback on 17th April 2025 
during the second Public Consultation Day for the scheme. The scheme 
received largely positive feedback and issues raised by the public have been 
taken into consideration.  This project is currently in Stage II, the planning 
process, where the preferred option is being developed and an application 
will be submitted to An Coimisiún Pleanála in 2026. 
Marlfield Lake FRS 
The ground investigation for the scheme was completed in January 2026 and 
samples taken during this have been sent for laboratory testing. The results 
will facilitate the Design Team in selecting the most appropriate design 
options for the Marlfield Flood Relief Scheme. Upon selection of the 
emerging preferred option, the scheme will then proceed to Stage II, the 
planning process, where the preferred option will be developed and an 
application submitted to An Coimisiún Pleanála. 
In parallel with the Capital FRS in Marlfield, work is continuing with the 
interim dam rehabilitation protection works involving various measures that 
will protect the existing dam and the surrounding area.  Undertaking work 
in Marlfield Lake area is complex with many environmental and statutory 
constraints, however we have been engaging with the relevant stakeholders, 
and significant progress has been made.  All the above is subject to OPW 
funding and approval.

Flood Relief Schemes 
Current Update 
Nenagh FRS 
The scope and complexity of the Nenagh Flood Relief Scheme has evolved 
significantly, and the scheme was formally reclassified in September 2023 
from a ‘small project’ to a major flood relief scheme. This decision reflects 
the scale of works required, the inclusion of critical infrastructure, and the 
need for robust governance and resources for a capital project of such 
magnitude. Preparatory work by the OPW has been ongoing with 
preliminary site surveys (topographical and CCTV) completed in Q4 2025. 
A Steering Group has been established to oversee delivery of the Nenagh 
FRS. 
Tender documents for the procurement of consultants to progress both the 
engineering and environmental elements of the scheme are currently being 
prepared. 
Stage I – Option Identification & Preliminary Design will commence 
following the procurement and appointment of the Design Team.  This is 
expected to progress in 2026 subject to OPW approval.

PUBLIC LIGHTING 
Operational Management 
 
The Roads Directorate continues to embed a 
digital operations and asset management platform. 
One-to-one training is ongoing with GSS’s and 
relevant staff.   
 
The system facilitates operational oversite and 
governance, reduces administrative time, delivers 
safety information and notices to the staff on the 
ground, and provides an auditable system for our 
Safety Management System and ISO 45001.  This 
transition now underpins our operations and safety 
management.  It has also identified opportunities 
for efficiency and improvements across other 
sections. 
 
The three core Roads Risk Assessment are 
currently being reviewed and will be combined in a 
single RA to allow the full integration of the digital 
platform and the SMS. 
 
 
For the assistance of members, if you need to 
report a public lighting fault, please contact the 
Customer Services Desk on 0818 06 5000, and 
they will log the fault.  Alternatively, you can log 
on via the links hereunder: 
 
https://www.deadsureapp.com/Inventory       
When the fault is logged in this format it will go 
straight to the hand-held device of our Public 
Lighting Contractor’s electrician for the 
area.  When reporting the fault, the following 
information should be provided:  
• 
The town/village/estate or street name  
• 
The number on the pole (identified in 
black located on a white background at eye 
level on the pole) 
• 
The location of the light (for example, 
outside house number 5) 
• 
A name and contact number.
